input.body:
label: bug
file: src/components/ExportButton.tsx

The Export button remains disabled after a failed export because the `handleClick` function does not reset the `busy` state if `exportReport` throws an error. The `setBusy(false)` call only runs in the `.then()` block, not in a `.catch()` handler.

input.title: Re-enable the export button after a failed export
input.body:
File: src/components/ExportButton.tsx

The `handleClick` function in the `ExportButton` component only resets the `busy` state to `false` when the `exportReport` promise resolves successfully. If the export fails (e.g., due to a non-2xx HTTP response), the `busy` state remains `true`, disabling the button permanently until a page reload. To fix this, the `.catch()` handler should also reset the `busy` state to `false` after showing an error toast, ensuring the button is re-enabled after a failed export.

input.body:
File: src/components/ExportButton.tsx

The `handleClick` function in the `ExportButton` component only resets the `busy` state to `false` when the `exportReport` promise resolves successfully. If the export fails (e.g., due to a non-2xx HTTP response), the `busy` state remains `true`, disabling the button permanently until a page reload. To fix this, the `.catch()` handler should also reset the `busy` state to `false` after showing an error toast, ensuring the button is re-enabled after a failed export.
